evidence.method: ITU-R BS.1770-4 4x oversampled polyphase FIR interpolation

learning_guide.what_was_detected: Your unmastered mix peaks at -0.4 dBTP with a limiter active on the master bus, leaving almost no headroom for mastering.
learning_guide.why_it_matters: Lossy encoders (Spotify OGG, Apple Music AAC, YouTube Opus) reconstruct continuous waveforms that clip audibly when True Peak exceeds -1.0 dBTP.
learning_guide.what_to_try: Bypass the brickwall limiter on your mix bus and lower the mix bus input trim by 3.5 dB so peaks sit safely between -6.0 and -3.0 dBTP.
learning_guide.how_to_verify: Export a 24-bit WAV bounce of Chorus 1 (00:42–00:58), re-upload it, and confirm True Peak reads at or below your target ceiling with zero audible crunch on snare hits.

issues.title: Momentary Stereo Phase Cancellation in Bridge (-0.18 correlation)

timestamps.label: Bridge Wide Synth Pad & Chorus Bass

learning_guide.what_was_detected: Between 01:48 and 02:04, the left and right channels pull out of phase (-0.18 correlation) when the widened synth pad and stereo bass chorus enter together.
learning_guide.why_it_matters: When played back on mono speakers (smart speakers, phone speakers, club PA systems), out-of-phase stereo signals partially cancel out, causing the synth and bass body to hollow out.
learning_guide.what_to_try: Use a Mid/Side EQ or stereo imaging plugin to keep frequencies below 140 Hz in mono, and reduce the stereo widener depth on the bridge pad by 20–30%.
learning_guide.how_to_verify: Toggle Mono Listening while looping 01:48–02:04. Verify that the bass and pad maintain steady volume and warmth when summed to mono.

issues.title: Warm Low-Mid Density in 200–500 Hz Band (-11.2 dBFS)

evidence.method: Welch Power Spectral Density integration (200-500 Hz)

learning_guide.what_was_detected: Energy between 200 Hz and 500 Hz is 2.8 dB higher than typical reference averages for this genre, creating a thick, warm lower-midrange balance.
learning_guide.why_it_matters: Rule 3 & 8 Note: This is a stylistic observation, not a technical defect. Depending on your artistic vision, a dense 250–400 Hz region can feel intimate and vintage, or it can slightly mask lead vocal intelligibility.
learning_guide.what_to_try: If you want extra vocal separation without losing warmth, try a gentle -1.5 dB dynamic EQ dip at 320 Hz on the rhythm guitar/keys bus triggered only when the lead vocal sings.
learning_guide.how_to_verify: Level-match before and after in the Verse (00:18–00:42) and listen for whether lead vocal consonants feel clearer while the guitars still sound full.

issues.title: Compact Loudness Range Across Arrangement (4.2 LU)

evidence.method: EBU Tech 3342 Loudness Range statistical distribution

learning_guide.what_was_detected: The loudness difference between verses and choruses measures 4.2 LU, indicating a consistently dense dynamic envelope from start to finish.
learning_guide.why_it_matters: Consistent loudness keeps energy steady in noisy environments, though a wider 6–8 LU contrast can make the chorus impact feel larger by comparison.
learning_guide.what_to_try: If you want the chorus entrance at 00:42.5 to hit harder, try automating the verse drum room and rhythm bus down by 1.0 to 1.5 dB during the final four bars of the pre-chorus.
learning_guide.how_to_verify: Play from 00:34 to 00:50 with your eyes closed and check whether the downbeat of Chorus 1 feels noticeably wider and taller.

recommendations.action_title: Restore 3–6 dB of Pre-Master True-Peak Headroom
recommendations.beginner_summary: Turn off your master bus limiter and lower your mix level so the loudest chorus peaks sit around -4 dB.
recommendations.advanced_dsp_guidance: Bypass Slot 3 (Brickwall True-Peak Limiter) on the stereo bus and apply -3.5 dB input trim ahead of the VCA Mix Bus Compressor so ITU-R BS.1770-4 True Peak stays <= -3.0 dBTP.
recommendations.verification_check: Re-upload Chorus 1 bounce and confirm True Peak Max <= -3.0 dBTP (Unmastered) or <= -1.0 dBTP (Master) with 0 sample clipping events.

recommendations.action_title: Stabilize Sub-140 Hz Mono Compatibility in Bridge
recommendations.beginner_summary: Keep your bass frequencies centered and slightly reduce the stereo widening effect on the bridge synth pad.
recommendations.advanced_dsp_guidance: Apply a 12 dB/oct Side-channel high-pass filter at 140 Hz on the synth/bass group during 01:48–02:04 so 100ms windowed correlation remains >= +0.15.
recommendations.verification_check: Check 01:48–02:04 in Mono Listening mode and verify no low-end drop occurs when toggling Stereo/Mono.

recommendations.action_title: Optional: Dynamic 320 Hz Pocket for Lead Vocal Clarity
recommendations.beginner_summary: If the lead vocal feels slightly buried in Verse 1, gently dip the warm midrange on the guitars/keys when the singer is active.
recommendations.advanced_dsp_guidance: Optional stylistic adjustment: Insert a sidechained dynamic bell (-1.5 dB max attenuation, Q=1.8 at 320 Hz) on the instrument bus keyed from the lead vocal stem.
recommendations.verification_check: Compare Verse 1 vocal intelligibility at matched LUFS loudness to confirm vocal presence improved without thinning the rhythm section.
